touches.text: Tool: a complete primitive. Has users, not an owner. Calls no other Cairn component (stdlib and base only) and owns no state of its own. Lives in cairn/tools/ (17). Its data for a holder lives under that holder: ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/tools/<tool>/.
Code that is no longer needed is deleted. Git history keeps it if we ever need it back.
help - the verb list with help strings; always human readable
Every verb anywhere is reached from the cairn command, as a path: cairn <device> [<machine> ...] <verb>. There is no central list.

help is defined once, as a root verb in the base shim, and answers exactly as `list` does: `help` is the word people type, `list` the system's word. It is readable cold (no bus, no device woken), so `cairn help` answers when nothing else is up. WHY: "help is specifically an anticipation of the behavior of the other monkeys in my species."

`cairn help` lists [all], then [operator], then [cairn], then every other device alphabetically. [all] is the verbs every device answers because the base shim defines them (help, stop, pause, ...), read from the base shim's verb table, never listed by hand.

The launcher walks the words. `cairn cairn foo bar` (the long form) means "tell the cairn device to run foo with argument bar". At each level: is the next word a machine here? Step into it and take the next word. Is it a script in this level's bin/? Run it, pass back the result, done. Neither? It is a bus verb: send it to this level over the bus. So `cairn foo bar baz`: foo is a device; it has a machine bar; bar's bin/ has baz, so baz runs. No bar machine? bar goes to foo over the bus. Each check is one directory lookup, so it is fast. WHY scripts first: scripts are the simple path; the bus is the route to what a device answers itself.
Owns the inspectors and gates (9.4): everything in the code pipeline that checks. The exception is diagnostic_inspector, which is base's (17.1).

Skills (skills/: cairnhelp, challenge, chart, commit, intent, sorted, ...) are Claude Code's. The deterministic parts move out of markdown into CC device verbs: a skill's OS-side work runs as a script, and CC's shim processes the result and injects it into the session. WHY: every habit captured that way is one CC no longer spends inference on, so CC gets faster; a first charting pass done in deterministic Python with no LLM until after saved about 90% of tokens, measured in real use.
edges: the frontier view: every charter's admitted gaps plus the open questions. [why?] USERS: CodeMother.
orient: the measuring scans before a build (where is X called, what's in each component). WHY: a build starts from what is, measured, not recalled. USERS: CodeMother's orient machine.
